record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Local limit as perceptual radius shrinks
record.original_question: For the nonlocal multispecies system ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − ∇·(u_i∇(Σ_j=1^n γ_ij u_j g,R)), do time-dependent or steady-state solutions remain well defined as the perceptual radius R tends to 0 from above, so that the nonlocal problem can be meaningfully connected to its local counterpart?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4. Do these solutions (either time-dependent or steady state) remain well-defined in the limit as R → 0+? In other words, can we meaningfully connect the nonlocal problem with its corresponding local problem in this limit?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded smooth domain (or the flat torus). For an integer $n \geq 1$, fix diffusion constants $d_i > 0$ and an interaction matrix $(\gamma_{ij})_{i,j=1}^n \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$. For each $R>0$, let $g_R: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be a radially symmetric, nonnegative averaging kernel of mean-zero radius $R$ (e.g., $g_R(x) = R^{-d} g_1(x/R)$ with $\int g_1 = 1$ and $\mathrm{supp}\, g_1 \subset \overline{B_1(0)}$), and define the spatial averaging operator
$$ (u \ast g_R)(x) = \int u(y)\, g_R(x-y)\, dy. $$

Consider the nonlocal multispecies advection–diffusion system
$$ \partial_t u_i \;=\; d_i \Delta u_i \;-\; \nabla \cdot \Big( u_i\, \nabla \big( \textstyle\sum_{j=1}^n \gamma_{ij}\, u_j \ast g_R \big) \Big), \qquad i = 1, \dots, n, $$
on $\Omega$, supplemented with no-flux (or periodic) boundary conditions and nonnegative initial data $u_i(0,\cdot) = u_i^0 \in L^\infty(\Omega)$.

Question: As the perceptual radius $R \to 0^+$, do the time-dependent (resp. steady-state) solutions $u^R = (u_1^R,\dots,u_n^R)$ remain well defined, and do they converge in a suitable function-space sense to solutions of the formally obtained local limit system
$$ \partial_t u_i \;=\; d_i \Delta u_i \;-\; \nabla \cdot \Big( u_i\, \nabla \big( \textstyle\sum_{j=1}^n \gamma_{ij}\, u_j \big) \Big)? $$

In other words, identify conditions on $(\gamma_{ij})$, $(d_i)$, and the initial data under which the family $\{u^R\}_{R>0}$ admits uniform a priori bounds enabling passage to the limit $R \to 0^+$, and prove that the limit solves the corresponding local cross-diffusion system.
artifact.status_search_result: The localisation limit ($R \to 0^+$) for nonlocal multispecies advection–diffusion / cross-diffusion systems of this type has been studied recently. In particular, work on "Multispecies cross-diffusions: from a nonlocal mean-field to a porous medium system" (arXiv:2306.01777, published in J. Differential Equations, 2024) proves convergence of the nonlocal system to a local cross-diffusion system as the interaction range tends to zero, under a full-rank assumption on the interaction kernels. Related existence theory by Giunta, Hillen, Lewis and Potts (SIADS, 2022) provides the uniform framework. Thus the question is partially resolved: localisation is established under structural hypotheses, but a complete answer covering all admissible coefficient matrices and steady-state solutions remains open.

status_evidence.title: Multispecies cross-diffusions: from a nonlocal mean-field to a porous medium system without self-diffusion
status_evidence.snippet: Localisation limit—convergence of nonlocal to local systems when the range of interaction tends to 0—proved under a full rank assumption on the interaction kernels.
status_evidence.claim: The R→0 limit linking the nonlocal system to a local cross-diffusion system has been rigorously established in a class of cases.

status_evidence.title: Local and Global Existence for Nonlocal Multispecies Advection-Diffusion Models (SIADS)
status_evidence.snippet: Existence theory for nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion models with finite perceptual radius kernels.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the well-posedness framework for the nonlocal R>0 problem needed for any limit analysis.
